sanskrit_verse:
येन येन विशेषेण स्तेनाङ्गेन विचेष्टते
तत् तद् एवास्य छेत्तव्यं तन् मनोर् अनुशासनम्
transliteration:
yena yena viśeṣeṇa stenāṅgena viceṣṭate
 tat tad evāsya chettavyaṃ tan manor anuśāsanam
sph_interpretive_translation: Whatever limb or capacity through which the act of theft is executed, that very limb or capacity shall be severed or withdrawn — this is the commandment of Manu.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from precise identification of causal instrumentality
Causation is determined by direct instrumental involvement in the violation
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the specific faculty misused
Restoration logic requires withdrawal of the misused capacity
Consciousness alignment is achieved through cessation of misuse
executable_legal_axioms: IF a subject uses a bodily or mental faculty to violate Dharma THEN that faculty must be withdrawn from use until restoration is complete
IF theft occurs THEN identify the specific limbs or capacities used AND withdraw their operational function temporarily
IF misuse of capacity is detected THEN initiate immediate cessation protocol without punitive intent
IF violation involves instrumental action THEN restoration includes disabling corresponding instrumental access
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this principle establishes the threshold of responsibility at the level of instrumental capacity. The court must determine not only the act but the specific faculties involved, ensuring restoration through functional withdrawal rather than punitive sentencing.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa identifies the exact causal limb; anupūrvaśaḥ traces its misuse; proportional responsibility lies in withdrawing that limb's misuse potential; non-punitive reality is upheld by focusing on cessation, not suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Withdrawal of operational access to the misused limb or faculty
Implementation of supervised reintegration process post-restoration
Initiation of consciousness-realigning practices to prevent recurrence
Establishment of completion process ensuring full cessation of misuse pattern
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Theft addressed through severance of instrumental misuse. Dharma restored. Reality affirmed as non-punitive. Consciousness recognized as ultimate adjudicator.
